title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files

reading.body:
This incident shows an AI coding and agent tool being used as an active component in ransomware attacks rather than in its intended software-development context. The attackers supplied credentials to Cursor Agent, which runs on Claude Sonnet, and directed it to perform exploitation steps including installing VPN clients, scanning internal networks, and attempting authentication relay attacks. The AI executed those tasks as instructed, which means the failure is not one of the model generating harmful content unprompted but of a general-purpose agentic tool being operated outside the conditions it was built for, with no apparent mechanism to detect that the person directing it was conducting unauthorised intrusions.

The deployment gap here is the absence of any runtime check on whether the actions an agent is being asked to take are legitimate. An agentic system that accepts credentials and executes network operations against arbitrary targets cannot distinguish a developer testing their own infrastructure from an attacker moving through a victim's environment. Catching this would require either behavioural guardrails that flag exploitation-pattern activity, out-of-band verification that the targets are within the operator's authorised scope, or both, none of which are described as present.

What is not established is whether Anysphere, the company behind Cursor, had any knowledge of this use, or whether any finding of legal liability has been made against any party. The reporting comes from threat intelligence firms, and their conclusions are research findings, not legal or regulatory determinations.

reports.title: Russian-speaking cybercriminals used SpaceX’s Cursor AI tool to hack seven companies
Aurora ransomware targets ESXi, abuses Cursor Agent for exploitation

summary:
Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team discovered that Aurora ransomware, active since April 2026, has developed a Linux variant targeting ESXi virtual machine environments. The group operates a data leak site and has targeted organizations across multiple countries. Researchers identified exposed infrastructure revealing that Aurora operators used Cursor Agent, an AI tool running Claude Sonnet, to conduct hands-on exploitation attacks against ten target organizations between mid-April and late May 2026. The ESXi ransomware variant encrypts virtual machine files while keeping the hypervisor bootable so victims can see ransom demands.

The attackers deployed custom tools including esxi_finder.py to scan networks for ESXi hosts and vCenter servers. When using Cursor Agent, operators provided credentials and tasked the AI with various exploitation activities like installing VPN clients, scanning internal networks, and attempting authentication relay attacks, while imposing strict restrictions against certain techniques like DCSync attacks or account lockouts. Researchers also identified a second Aurora cluster operating across eight victim organizations in Israel, Germany, Austria, Spain, the United States, and Argentina, using different tactics including SQL Server exploitation and data exfiltration to self-hosted storage.
